name: Chevrolet Corvette Z06 (C8)
engine: 5.5L naturally aspirated flat-plane V8 (LT6, DOHC 32-valve, dry-sump), 8,600 rpm redline
curb_weight: ~3,600 lbs (3,434 dry with Z07 + carbon wheels)
reliability: 6/10 - the LT6 is an engineering jewel: the most powerful naturally aspirated V8 ever put in a production car, hand-assembled at GM's Bowling Green Performance Build Center. But early-build 2023 cars have real teething problems - a known front timing-cover oil leak whose one-time-use aluminum bolts were backordered for months, plus a handful of outright engine failures replaced under warranty. The car is fundamentally sound and heavily warrantied; the smart move is a later-build or already-sorted example.
cost_to_own: Insurance: Very High (supercar pace, six-figure value, theft and appreciation) - the flat-plane V8 wants ~8 qt of dexos-R 5W-50 full synthetic, carbon-wheel cars are hard to service (dealers struggle to seat the run-flats), and it drinks fuel (~14-15 mpg combined) from a small 18.5-gal tank. Budget like an exotic, not a Corvette.
popular_mods: Cat-back / axle-back exhaust to unleash the flat-plane V8's F1-like wail
ECU calibration and intake work (limited NA headroom - the LT6 is already near the edge)
Track alignment, pads, and high-temp fluid to match the Z07 aero package
Aftermarket wheels to escape the fragile, hard-to-service carbon setup
Aero and cooling upgrades for sustained track use
oil_type: 5W-50 full synthetic (Mobil 1, GM dexos-R; dry-sump, ~8 qt)

generations.C5 Z06 (2001-2004): The Z06 name reborn - LS6 5.7L, lightweight fixed-roof hardtop, the affordable-performance icon.
generations.C6 Z06 (2006-2013): LS7 7.0L naturally aspirated with a dry sump, ~505 hp - the last big-inch NA Z06.
generations.C7 Z06 (2015-2019): Supercharged LT4 6.2L, 650 hp - brutally fast, if heat-soak-prone on track.
generations.C8 Z06 (2023-present): This car. Mid-engine, with an all-new LT6 5.5L flat-plane V8 - 670 hp at 8,400 rpm, an 8,600 rpm redline, and the title of most powerful naturally aspirated V8 in any production car. 8-speed dual-clutch, RWD.

common_issues: LT6 front timing-cover oil leak - a known early-build defect; the one-time-use aluminum bolts were backordered, stranding some cars for weeks
Isolated LT6 engine failures on early 2023 cars (ticking/knock, lockup) replaced under warranty
8-speed dual-clutch gasket leaks and transient error messages on some cars
Carbon-fiber wheels with run-flat tires are hard to service - many dealers can't seat the tires
Long delivery delays and constrained carbon-fiber parts supply on early cars
maintenance_tips: Prefer a later-build or already-sorted car; confirm the timing-cover leak fix and any TSBs were completed
Use the specified dexos-R 5W-50 full synthetic and keep intervals short with track use - the dry sump revs to 8,600
Warm the engine fully before using the top of the rev range; let it cool after hard laps
Plan tire service around the carbon-wheel / run-flat quirk - use a shop that has actually done it
Lean on the factory warranty for the LT6 - it covers the early-build engine risks

engine.detail: LT6 - 5.5L naturally aspirated flat-plane-crank V8, DOHC 32-valve with a dry-sump oiling system, an active split intake with twin 87 mm throttle bodies, and forged titanium rods. 670 hp at 8,400 rpm to an 8,600 rpm redline: the most powerful NA V8 ever in a production car, hand-built at Bowling Green.
engine.watch: Early 2023 builds have a known front timing-cover oil leak (backordered bolts) and a few warranty engine replacements - buy sorted, keep the warranty, and run dexos-R 5W-50.

drivetrain.detail: 8-speed Tremec TR-9080 dual-clutch transaxle behind the mid-mounted V8, driving the rear wheels through a short 5.56 final drive - 0-60 in about 2.6 seconds with the Z07 package.
drivetrain.watch: Some cars show dual-clutch gasket leaks and transient error messages; service the transaxle fluid on schedule.

suspension.detail: Magnetic Ride Control 4.0 on a track 3.6 inches wider than the Stingray, with an available Z07 package adding stiffer springs, carbon-ceramic brakes, and aggressive aero for genuine downforce.
suspension.watch: Z07 cars ride firm and wear pads and tires quickly on track; alignment is fussy after any suspension work.

brakes.detail: Big Brembo brakes with available carbon-ceramic rotors (Z07) for repeated high-speed stops with minimal fade.
brakes.watch: Carbon-ceramics are exotic-car expensive to replace, and the carbon wheels make tire and brake service harder.

fuel.detail: Direct-injected, high-revving NA V8 with an active split intake manifold - power comes from revs and airflow, not boost.
fuel.watch: Real-world economy is ~14-15 mpg combined from an 18.5-gallon tank, so range is short; it wants premium fuel.

body.detail: Mid-engine composite-and-aluminum body 3.6 inches wider than the Stingray, with available carbon-fiber wheels and Z07 aero (front splitter, big rear wing) making real downforce.
body.watch: Front-end and splitter stone chips; carbon parts are costly, and early cars saw carbon-fiber supply delays.
